_comment: How each official SDK is driven by the conformance harness, and which canonical
`export` runs in the SDK's own directory with two environment variables set:
FRAISEQL_CONFORMANCE_OUT      absolute path to write schema.json to
It must author the fixture through the SDK's PUBLIC authoring API — never by
hand-assembling the expected JSON. Six of the eleven pre-existing parity generators
did exactly that and were therefore incapable of failing.
`unsupported` maps a construct name to the reason the SDK cannot author it. The
default is that every construct is required: adding one to project.CONSTRUCTS fails
every SDK until each either implements it or declares the gap here. Declaring a gap
is deliberate and public — README.md renders these reasons into the support matrix.
A declaration that is no longer true also fails, so the matrix cannot go stale.

unsupported.subscriptions: the SDK ships no subscription authoring surface at all — no builder, no decorator, no registry entry. Five of the eleven SDKs have one (Python, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Java); adding a sixth is a feature, not a key rename, so the gap is declared rather than papered over (#1024).
